doc.title: Buddy Collette interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 13, 1999

title: First jazz influences: jamming friends, radio bands, Louis Armstrong
summary: He recalls musicians jamming at home and hearing Ellington, Lunceford, Basie and Armstrong.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: Do you recall hearing, was there a certain kind of music that inspired you to go in the direction of jazz that you might have heard early on?

Yes I think so. There were a couple of friends of my mother and dad that used to come by and one guy was a piano player and one a saxophone player. They’d come by and just jam two or three days a week since I guess they only worked at night. They’d come by to practice, we always had a piano. And so I heard these guys jamming a lot. And that was something, and plus the Ellington band and Jimmy Lunceford and Count Basie band more later on, I got a chance to hear them, they were on the radio a lot and playing in clubs. And my mother and dad took us to hear Louis Armstrong when I was about ten to twelve, so when you hear that sound, especially then, whew, I seen him just one time and that was it.
